title: How long does a catch take?
hook: A falling ruler can time a reaction. How long does a catch really take?

knows: things speed up as they fall
doesNotKnow: how to turn a fall distance into a time with d = 1/2 g t²

misconception: Reaction time is negligible, or about a second.
objective: The learner can explain that a ruler caught after a fall of about 20 cm shows a reaction time of about 0.2 s, because fall distance grows with the square of time.

claims.text: A ruler falling from rest drops a distance d = 1/2 g t² in time t, so a catch at distance d shows a reaction time t = √(2d / g).
claims.source: Constant-acceleration kinematics from rest; g = 9.81 m/s². No air drag (negligible for a ruler over 20 cm).

claims.text: A catch at 20 cm means t = √(2 × 0.20 / 9.81) = 0.20 s. (Reveal: 'for 20 cm, t = √(2 × 0.200 m ÷ 9.81) = 0.20 s', the stage's working-line format.)
claims.source: Recomputed in node: Math.sqrt(0.4 / 9.81) = 0.2019 s (Demo.tsx timeFor). | Builder revision v3 (demo-builder, 2026-10-14): (r7) The time scale is now drawn only after the commit (it put 0.20 s beside 20 cm on the locked stage), and the reveal writes out the conversion in the same form as the new stage working line. Builder statement, not self-verified. | FC pass 26 (fact-checker, 2026-10-14): working(20) = 't = sqrt(2 x 0.200 m / 9.81) = 0.20 s' (node; timeFor(20) = 0.20193). Inverse check: 0.5 x 9.81 x t^2 x 100 = 20 cm exactly. Time scale is drawn only when unlocked; reveal string is the same function as the stage working line.

claims.text: Typical human visual reaction time is about 0.2 to 0.25 s.
claims.source: Woods et al. 2015, Factors influencing the latency of simple reaction time, Front. Hum. Neurosci. 9:131; Kosinski 2008, A Literature Review on Reaction Time (Clemson University). Not in the reveal text; informs the simulated catcher's mean of 0.20 s. | Earlier text: 'TO CITE: a measured-reaction-time reference (for example a physiology or ruler-drop practical text). Not in the reveal text; informs the simulated catcher's mean of 0.20 s.' | FACT-CHECK 2026-10-13: Support found: Kosinski, A Literature Review on Reaction Time (Clemson, 2008, quoting Galton and others) gives visual reaction times of 180-200 ms; Woods et al. 2015, Front. Hum. Neurosci. 9:131 report Galton's visual simple RT below 190 ms and longer, hardware-dependent values in modern samples; screen-based medians for ages 15-24 are about 220-250 ms. Suggested source text: cite Woods et al. 2015 and Kosinski 2008 instead of 'TO CITE'. · v4 (2026-10-14, demo-builder, W-095): the fact-checker's suggested references now replace 'TO CITE'; builder did not open the papers. Previous verdict void; needs re-check. | FC pass 35 (fact-checker, 2026-10-14): HELD. Woods et al. 2015 and Kosinski 2008 could not be opened from this host (web blocked). Not in learner text; it informs the simulated mean of 0.20 s. | FC pass 38 (fact-checker, 2026-10-14): HELD (not in learner text). No source that supports it could be opened from this host: the cited hosts return proxy 403 or fail DNS, and only GitHub raw, PyPI and npm are reachable. I did not verify it from memory or from search snippets. Woods et al. 2015 (Front. Hum. Neurosci.) and Kosinski 2008 (Clemson) were not opened.
claims.note: FC pass 41 (fact-checker, 2026-10-15): VERIFIED. Not learner-visible (informs the simulated mean of 0.20 s). Opened on PMC: Woods et al. (2015), 'Factors influencing the latency of simple reaction time', Front Hum Neurosci 9: 131 (PMC4374455). Abstract: Galton 'reported visual SRT latencies below 190 ms in young subjects', and in 1,469 subjects aged 18-65 'Mean SRT latencies were short (231, 213 ms when corrected for hardware delays)'. Corrected 'true' SRTs 'ranged from 200 ms in the youngest subject group to 222 ms in the oldest', and recent computer-based means run from 233 ms upward. 'About 0.2 to 0.25 s' for a simple visual reaction fits. Kosinski 2008 is not opened and not needed.

claims.text: The catcher is simulated: reaction times are drawn from a seeded random spread (seed 1) around 0.20 s, and the stage does not time the learner's own reflex.
claims.source: Demo.tsx: MEAN_T 0.20 s, SPREAD 0.05 s as the sum of three uniforms minus 1.5, SEED 1. Seed 1 was the first tried; seeds 2 and 3 give similar means (about 20 cm). Stated on stage ('Simulated catcher').

claims.text: Near a 20 cm catch, each extra centimetre of fall is about 5 thousandths of a second (so a ruler resolves hundredths of a second).
claims.source: Node: timeFor(21 cm) - timeFor(20 cm) = 0.2069 - 0.2019 = 0.0050 s. · v4 (2026-10-14, demo-builder, learner r8): sentence cut from the reveal ('near 20 cm, each extra centimetre is about 5 thousandths of a second'); told context, word budget (learner r8). Withdrawn, not learner-visible.

claims.text: The learner's own catches (between the smallest and largest distances caught so far) convert to times by the same formula. (Stage: a working line 'x cm: t = √(2 × d m ÷ 9.81) = t s' for the latest catch, and a 'Seen: N catches, lo to hi cm = t_lo to t_hi s' row that Clear does not erase.)
claims.source: Reveal computes min, max of the learner's catches from TRIALS and converts each with timeFor. | Builder revision v3 (demo-builder, 2026-10-14): (r7) Added the working line (working(cm) = 't = √(2 × cm/100 m ÷ 9.81) = timeFor(cm) s', two decimals as on the readout) and the persistent Seen row; the reveal quotes the Seen row. Title and hook no longer say 'your reflex' or 'blink-quick' (the catcher is simulated; 'blink-quick' pointed at a short time). Builder statement, not self-verified. | FC pass 26 (fact-checker, 2026-10-14): Own mulberry32 port, seed 1 (fc26-b0/ruler.mjs): TRIALS 16.4, 27.4, 22.2, 24.2, 13.3, 12.6, ...; every catch converts with timeFor (inverse exact). Seen row after 5 drops 'Seen: 5 catches, 13.3 to 27.4 cm = 0.16 to 0.24 s', after 6 '12.6 to 27.4 cm = 0.16 to 0.24 s'. seen is max catches on the ruler at once and Clear only sets n = 0, so the row survives Clear; drops after Clear replay the same TRIALS, so lo/hi stay the learner's catches. The working line uses lastCm = TRIALS[next - 1], the latest catch. The reveal needs milestone five, so seen >= 5.

claims.text: The simulated ruler falls from rest with no air drag (stage caption: 'Simulated catcher, not your reflex. The ruler falls from rest, no air drag.').
claims.source: Demo.tsx fallCm(t) = 50 g t² (d = ½ g t², no drag term). v4 (2026-10-14, demo-builder): 'no air drag' moved from the reveal ('No air drag; the catcher here is simulated.', cut for the word budget) into the stage caption. Needs check. | FC pass 35 (fact-checker, 2026-10-14): VERIFIED. fallCm(t) = 50 g t^2 = 100 x g t^2/2, no drag term; caption after the commit reads exactly 'Simulated catcher, not your reflex. The ruler falls from rest, no air drag.'

recall.question: A ruler is caught after falling 45 cm. Compared with a 20 cm catch, that reaction was...
recall.why: t = √(2 × 0.45 / 9.81) = 0.30 s, against 0.20 s for 20 cm. More fall means a longer wait, but distance grows with time squared.
